newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy puts troops on stand-by for Albania - agency.
newsitem.headline: Italy puts troops on stand-by for Albania - agency.

text.p: Italy is moving 800 troops to the southeast port of Brindisi in case they are required for deployment in Albania as part of a European Union relief mission, the news agency ANSA reported on Friday.

The unsourced but detailed report said the soldiers, who included members of two crack paratroop regiments and two armoured units, were being relocated to Brindisi, mainly from the west coast port of Livorno.

ANSA said they would be on stand-by to link up with Italian naval and air forces if European Union foreign ministers meeting in Brussels next Monday decided that a security force would be needed to assist a humanitarian relief mission to Albania.
The Defence Ministry has denied persistent media reports in the past few days of impending Italian military intervention in Albania but had no immediate comment on the ANSA story.
"All I can confirm is that we are waiting for the European Union to meet and we hope it will take a decision soon," one official said.
Albania's new national unity government, formed last week in response to an armed rebellion in the south, has asked the EU to help restore order and provide food and medical relief.

Prime Minister Bashkim Fino wants an international peacekeeping force to be sent to Albania to help to restore law and order after weeks of civil unrest, but the EU has indicated it would not back any large-scale military intervention.

The head of an EU team that visited Albania this week, Dutch diplomat Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, said after his return from Tirana on Wednesday that Europe should send a "modest police presence" to the Balkan state.
The ANSA report said Italian armed forces were making contingency plans to go to Albania if required.
"These are preparations for making military units available to the European Union as part of a multinational force," it said.
It said Italian military planners had identified three Albanian beaches where landings could be staged.
Italian diplomatic sources said earlier on Friday that they expected some foreign police contingent would be needed to accompany any relief mission to Albania.
